family.tagline: A baby, two parents and one Companion Core in a cottage with a garden nook.
family.story: Wanjiru writes software from the glass garden nook beside the living room. Juma stays home with baby Zuri and grows vegetables outside. One Companion Core on the living-room shelf keeps their code, lists, pictures and plants.

companion.name: Rowan
companion.job: Drafts talk outlines from the bullet notes Wanjiru sends it.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Wanjiru rewrites every outline in her own words.

members.name: Juma
members.work: at home with Zuri, grows vegetables

companion.name: Biscuit
companion.job: Drafts Juma’s posts for the neighbourhood seedling swap.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Juma reads each post and sends it himself.

popup.title: Wanjiru carries the parcel in
popup.body: A parcel with a Companion Core waits at the foot of the porch steps. Wanjiru carries it in, and Juma clears the living-room shelf.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Juma reads the guide aloud while Zuri crumples the packing paper.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Wanjiru plugs in the cable. Juma presses the button, and the Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: On his phone, Juma joins the Core’s own network, then chooses the home network.

popup.title: Pick the first agents and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Juma picks Hermes. Wanjiru adds Gitea and Home Assistant. Wanjiru and Juma name the agents Rowan and Biscuit, then walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Juma says hello to Biscuit
popup.body: From the loveseat, Juma messages the agent he named Biscuit. It answers from the Core, and the first job is seeds.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: juma
say.text: Hello, Juma. I am Biscuit. Shall we start with seeds?

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: Both camera rolls become one album
popup.body: Zuri’s first months sit on two phones. On the loveseat, Juma and Wanjiru gather them into one Immich album on the Core.
popup.note: The first start takes a while.

beats.capability: back up your files with encryption, to a local disk beside your Core

popup.title: A deleted folder comes back
popup.body: Wanjiru deletes the wrong folder by mistake. The encrypted copy Duplicati keeps on a disk beside the Core brings it back.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally

popup.title: One tap before the afternoon walk
popup.body: Pram ready, Juma taps one scene. The lamps and the kettle plug go off together. Home Assistant, which needs no cloud account, runs the scene from the Core.

beats.capability: host private Git repositories, pull requests and issues on your Core

popup.title: Naptime is code time
popup.body: While Zuri naps, Wanjiru merges her talk demo branch in Gitea. Its issues and pull requests sit with the code on the Core.

beats.capability: connect your apps with workflows, with the data staying on your Core

popup.title: The nook lamp keeps office hours
popup.body: Each weekday at nine, Wanjiru’s n8n workflow lights the nook lamp through Home Assistant. It runs on the Core, so the data does not pass through a connector service.

beats.capability: an agent that talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Wanjiru rewrites Rowan’s outline
popup.body: Wanjiru messages Rowan her bullet notes for a meetup talk. Rowan drafts an outline on the Core’s local model, and Wanjiru rewrites it in her own words.
popup.note: Companion Agents are in beta. Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: wanjiru
say.text: Outline done. Cut what you like, then write it your way.

beats.capability: take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server

popup.title: A note holds the colour code
popup.body: A scuff in the hall needs touch-up paint. Wanjiru finds the colour code in an old note at the trestle table. Her notes sync to Joplin Server on the Core.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: The brown leaf has a history
popup.body: A leaf on the peace lily has browned. Juma checks its HortusFox page: last watered ten days ago. He fills the can and logs the date.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book and meal planner for the household

popup.title: The paper list leaves the fridge
popup.body: Juma copies the paper list from the fridge door into KitchenOwl: rice, cardamom, nappies. The same list reaches Wanjiru’s phone from the Core.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book and meal planner for the household

popup.title: Wednesday’s greens come from the garden
popup.body: For Wednesday, Juma puts sukuma wiki on the meal plan in KitchenOwl. The greens come from the garden, so he leaves them off the shopping list.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: Thursday’s call moves lunch to Juma
popup.body: Wanjiru adds a Thursday call to the family calendar in Nextcloud. Juma sees it on his phone, served from the Core, and takes over the lunch job.

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off

popup.title: Zuri sleeps halfway through a rhyme
popup.body: After the morning feed, Zuri falls asleep in the glider halfway through a rhyme podcast. Audiobookshelf keeps the place, and the episodes are downloaded to the Core.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history, with photos and a garden journal

popup.title: Last year’s journal picks the spot
popup.body: Beside the pergola deck, Juma checks last year’s HortusFox journal to choose where the beans climb. The journal stays on the Core.

beats.capability: read ebooks in your browser, with notes and highlights; your library lives on your Core

popup.title: Wanjiru reads on the patio
popup.body: At lunch on a patio lounger, Wanjiru reads a programming book from her own library in Koodo Reader. The library is stored on the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that talks to you through the messaging platform you pick

popup.title: Juma posts the seedling swap himself
popup.body: Juma messages Biscuit the seedlings he has spare. Biscuit drafts a post for the neighbourhood swap on the Core’s local model. Juma reads it and posts it himself.
popup.note: Companion Agents are in beta. Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: juma
say.text: Here is the swap post. Read it, then post it when you are ready.

popup.title: One Core in the garden cottage
popup.body: Code, lists, plants and a baby’s first months sit on one Companion Core in a small garden cottage.

closing.body: Your code, shopping lists, pictures and plants can sit on one Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store, and pick the first apps for your house.

notes: The Garden Nook has no desk item. Wanjiru's beats anchor on room:office and the text names what the nook has: a rattan armchair, a lamp, a bird of paradise.
No TV and no kitchen island in this home. The couch media beat is the Immich album on the loveseat; the kitchen beats anchor on the fridge, the range and the counter.
The validator wants one beat for a member under thirteen, so Zuri owns nursery-rhymes; she is otherwise seen through her parents' beats.
Duplicati names a disk beside the Core (catalog cloud-link caveat: name a local disk). The restore is told as the point of a backup, with no reliability claim.
Both companions are Hermes. All three Hermes beats carry the chat-service note; the two later ones add the Companion Agents beta line.
Garden walk: the pergola deck at the rear, the east patio loungers, then the front shrub bed beside the street.
Code Server and Ollama have no QA screenshot and are not used. Open WebUI, Paperless-ngx, VaultWarden and Yuvomi are left out: the fleet already names them in over 40 percent of families.
The phone popups (ftue-join, ftue-pick) are not in the film.
